sentences.text: JUDGMENT
Heard Sri Sanganagouda V.Biradar, learned counsel for the appellants in both the appeals as well as Sri S.S.Aspalli, learned counsel who is representing the Insurance Company in both the appeals.
Notice to other respondents stood dispensed with.

2. Challenge in both these appeals is the common order that is rendered by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-V, Vijayapura in M.V.C.No.728/2016 and M.V.C.No.729/2016 dated 26.11.2020.
3.

The case of the appellants in nutshell is that on 16.09.2016 while they were proceeding on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-28/EJ-4147 on Dandaragi - Vijayapura road as a pillion riders while one Appasab was riding the motorcycle, a lorry being driven by its driver at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner dashed against their NC: 2024:KHC-K:3031 motorcycle from opposite direction, due to which they fell down and sustained injuries.

4. Sri Sanganagouda V.Biradar, learned counsel for the appellants submits that the appellant in M.F.A.No.202605/2022 sustained fracture for right radius bone and fracture of first metacarpal bone of which are grievous in nature.
Learned counsel states that the Doctor who was examined stated that the disability is about 15% to 20% of right upper limb.
Learned counsel also contends that the claimant took treatment as inpatient and incurred huge expenditure.
But the Tribunal awarded a meager sum of Rs.1,52,114/- as compensation which is highly unjustifiable.
Learned counsel also submits that despite taking extensive treatment the claimant is suffering with disability and therefore just amount may be awarded as compensation.

A perusal of the impugned order reveals that the Tribunal having taken the percentage of disability in respect of whole body as 7%,
has awarded the compensation under the following heads :
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3031 1. Towards pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
already undergone and to be suffered in future mental and physical shock hardship inconvenience and discomfort etc. towards loss of amenities in life and account of disability.

2. Towards attendants charges Rs.1,600/-
3.

Towards medical expenses Rs.50,514/-
Total Rs.1,52,114/-
5. However, as rightly contended, the Tribunal failed to award any sum towards conveyance charges and loss of income during laid-up period.

Also the amount awarded towards attendant charges i.e.,
Rs.1,600/- is grossly low.

6. Having considered the aspect of the disability as observed by the Tribunal to be 7% and as the Yashavant vs Mr. Irphan And Ors on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154798663/

sentences.text: right hand of the claimant is effected due to the injuries sustained, as it is established that a sum of Rs.50,514/- was incurred towards medical expenses for the treatment taken, this Court is of the view that just amount which the claimant is entitled to under all heads which includes pain and NC:

2024 :KHC-K:3031 suffering, mental agony, hardship and inconvenience caused during the period of treatment and due to disability thereafter, loss of amenities in life, loss of earnings both during laid-up period and future, attendant charges and medical expenses
would be a sum of Rs.2,50,000/-.
The said sum in the humble opinion of this Court is just and reasonable.
7. Coming to the other appeal i.e., the appeal in M.F.A.No.202606/2022, the appellant therein admittedly sustained three simple injuries.
It is not in dispute that the appellant took treatment as inpatient for eight days.

Further, it is not in dispute that the appellant incurred a sum of Rs.21,085/-
towards medical expenses.
The Tribunal on all count awarded compensation of Rs.32,685/- under the following heads :-

1. Towards pain and suffering Rs.10,000/-
2.

Towards medical expenses Rs.21,085/-
3.
Towards attendant charges Rs.1,600/-

However, having considered the period of treatment taken and as no amount is awarded under the head 'loss of earnings',
'conveyance charges' etc., and as it is observed by this Court that even the amount awarded towards 'pain and sufferings' is low, this Court is of the view that a sum of Rs.50,000/- in total is required to be awarded as the same would be just and reasonable compensation.
9.

In view of the foregoing discussion, the following :
ORDER i) Both the appeals are allowed in part.

ii) The amount awarded as compensation by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-V,
Vijayapura through orders in M.V.C.No.728/2016 is enhanced from Rs.1,52,114/- to Rs.2,50,000/-.
